$description:
THERE IS NO HEIGHT RAMP HERE ANY MORE. `control-height` (28/32/40/48px) was deleted on 2026-08-14 and nothing replaced it: an input, a button or a select is now as tall as its padding plus its text, and no token states a height.

The reason is that a fixed px height cannot grow with its contents. The text inside these elements is sized in `rem` via a `clamp()`, so it grows with a user's browser font-size preference, with a spoke's taller face, or when a translation wraps — and a px box cannot follow. `esa-text-field` paired that fixed height with `overflow: hidden`, so what did not fit was silently cut, which is WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize text). Padding cannot fail that way: whatever the line box turns out to be, the padding still surrounds it.

What replaced the ramp is padding — but NOT a padding token. `--form-padding-y-*` and `--form-padding-x-*` held that role for a few hours on the same day and was deleted too (migrations.json: form-padding-to-spacing): it was a flat passthrough to `--spacing-200/250/300/400`, identical on both axes, that nothing ever re-pointed. The eleven controls read those spacing rungs directly, as 31 other components already did. The consequence to be clear about is that there is now NO one-line density lever for a spoke: re-declaring the old padding name does nothing, and re-pointing `--spacing-*` moves every gap in the kit, because it is a CORE set. Tightening the controls is a /request-lego. Consequence worth knowing: because the type is fluid, the heights are now fluid too. An input is roughly 38px on a phone and 41px on a wide monitor rather than 40px everywhere. A row still aligns, because siblings on the same size step share a padding value and a type rung, so they resolve to the same height.

See typography-migration-log.md Change 9. Do not re-add a height token; if something looks wrong, the padding is the thing to change.

chip-height.$description:
The size scale for badges and pills — labels that sit inline with text rather than things you click. Deliberately its own ramp, and deliberately still FIXED, which is now the exception in this file rather than the rule.

It stays fixed because a badge is a shape more than a box of text: every badge in the kit is the same height whatever its label, and a padding-sized one could not line up with the others on a row. The tradeoff is the one the height ramp was deleted for — these will clip if their text outgrows them — but they carry `line-height: var(--line-height-none)` and no `overflow: hidden`, so overgrown text spills visibly instead of being cropped silently.

NOTE for the batched accessibility pass: `xs` (18px) and `sm` (22px) are below the WCAG 2.5.8 AA minimum of 24px, and esa-chip-group is interactive. Pre-existing, recorded rather than fixed.
